create.name: Josh Korda
create.bio:
Since 2005 Josh Korda has led Dharma Punx NYC + Brooklyn as its guiding teacher. The community is secular and Buddhist in outlook, belongs to no larger organisation and runs on donations, and he serves it as a Buddhist pastor, offering one-to-one spiritual counselling alongside his public teaching. He came to the dharma after a career in advertising, which he left in the years after the September 2001 attacks, and his teaching pairs early Buddhist practice with what modern psychology has learned about attachment, emotion and the way people relate to one another.

He leads a weekly Tuesday evening class on Zoom, meets students in person once a month in Williamsburg, and holds an annual Labor Day weekend retreat at the Garrison Institute in the Hudson Valley, together with fellow teacher Kathy Cherry. His evening talks have been released as a free podcast for many years, and the archive now runs to more than eight hundred episodes. His book Unsubscribe: Opt Out of Delusion, Tune In to Truth came out from Wisdom Publications in 2017, and he has written essays for Tricycle, Lion's Roar and Buddhadharma. For more than ten years he has also spoken to trainee hospice volunteers at ZenCare, a non-profit caregiving project.

books.title: Unsubscribe: Opt Out of Delusion, Tune In to Truth
books.author: Josh Korda
books.description: Josh Korda's account of stepping back from a life built around consumption and status, set out in three stages: finding a purpose worth living for, getting to know your own emotional needs, and building honest, secure relationships. Buddhist teaching sits alongside his own story and exercises readers can try.

free_resources.title: Dharmapunx NYC podcast (Josh Korda's talks)
free_resources.description: Recordings of Josh's weekly dharma talks, released for many years and now numbering over eight hundred episodes, with new talks added most weeks. Free to stream or download.

free_resources.title: Josh Korda on Insight Timer
free_resources.description: Guided meditations and talk-and-practice sessions drawn from Buddhist sources, among them breath meditation, emptiness practice and the RAIN method for meeting emotions. Free to listen to in the app or on the web.

free_resources.title: Dharma Punx NYC retreat recordings
free_resources.description: Talks and guided meditations from past Garrison Institute retreats taught by Josh with Jessica Morey, plus chants from the community's retreats. Each recording can be downloaded free.

free_resources.title: Unsubscribe, chapter one (free PDF)
free_resources.description: The opening chapter of his book, on making meaning rather than chasing comfort, offered as a free download on the Dharma Punx NYC site.

sprint.tier_evidence: Insight Timer 13.2k (profile, 1 Nov 2026); YouTube @joshkorda8809 903 subscribers (channel header, 1 Nov 2026); Instagram @joshkorda 4,128 (og:description, 1 Nov 2026); Dharma Punx NYC Instagram 5,305 and podcast downloads (6M) not counted (community account / podcast audience); no Facebook or X found → ~18.2k total → local_hero
flags: Email dpxnyc@gmail.com is the Dharma Punx NYC community inbox (mailto in the site footer and podcast notes), not a personal address.
Instagram @joshkorda (name 'Josh Korda', 4.1k) is not linked from his site; it looks like him but is not confirmed, and is counted and linked on that basis.

Recovery framing, borderline: Josh speaks openly about his own past addiction, the Amazon blurb for Unsubscribe calls it a guide to 'recovery from addiction to consumerism', he led an 11th Step retreat (April 2026, past) and some podcast episodes deal with addictive behaviour. Kept because his site and teaching as a whole are general secular dharma; the book is described without that framing.

Political check: the Dharma Punx NYC home page carries a quote from him calling on people to stand as allies 'in the resistance against brutality and oppression against people of color' (the Kerri Kelly precedent held a listing for the owner's political check).
His Insight Timer bio describes his counselling as 'attachment based'; the bio here says spiritual counselling only and lists no conditions.
No current offerings with their own URL: the weekly Tuesday class is a Zoom link on the home page, all 2026 calendar events are past, and the Patreon tiers can't be read without logging in.

Videos: his own YouTube channel is mostly his electronic and piano music; three teaching videos come from it, the rest are on other channels (Lion's Roar, unself TV, Garrison Institute, What Meditation Really Is, marksand, Francesca Maximé) where he is the main speaker or one of two in a dialogue (the Lion's Roar and Garrison videos are conversations with Koshin Paley Ellison).
Availability local_online with New York as the base: in-person class is in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, once a month; retreats are at the Garrison Institute.
left_out: Weekly Tuesday Zoom class and monthly Williamsburg class: no page of its own (Zoom link on the home page).
Patreon membership (patreon.com/dharmapunxnyc): tiers and prices not readable without logging in; it is framed as support for his pastoral work.

2026 retreats on the Dharma Punx calendar (Garrison Labor Day 4–7 Sep, Omega Buddhist Summer Camp May, 11th Step retreat April, Kathy Cherry's Awakening the Body events): all past or led by Kathy Cherry.
Podcast and interview videos with recovery or healing framing (Recovery Happy Hour, The Healing Journey with Chris Grosso, Friends Health Connection, Garrison 'Budismo e recuperação'): health rule.
YouTube 'the gradual path' and 'self-soothing' on his own channel: could not tell whether they are teaching or music; the channel is mostly music tracks.
Insight Timer tracks titled for intrusive thoughts and insecure attachment: not listed (profile link covers tracks; condition-framed).
CBS News 'Not Your Mother's Meditation' segment: a news piece about him, not his teaching.
